studies.title: Female Sexual Desire, Arousal, and Orgasmic Dysfunctions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Treatment Options.
studies.abstract: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of treatments for female sexual desire, arousal, and orgasmic dysfunction in patients without sexual pain conditions. MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and ClinicalTrials.gov. Following the initial search in December 2024, a total of 8994 abstracts were screened, 278 full-text articles were reviewed, and 36 studies met criteria for data abstraction including a patient population with female sexual dysfunction (FSD) of desire, arousal, and/or orgasm (DAO) and outcome measures including the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), its DAO subscales, and the Female Sexual Distress Scale (FSDS). Studies including patients with sexual pain conditions were excluded. Two reviewers independently conducted each phase. Of the 36 studies, 26 were RCTs and 10 were single-arm trials. Ten studies evaluated cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), 24 investigated medication therapy, and 2 investigated devices. Meta-analyses were conducted for mindfulness-based CBT, flibanserin, and bremelanotide. Mindfulness-based CBT significantly improved total FSFI and subscales of desire, arousal, and orgasm. Conversely, flibanserin improved total FSFI and desire while bremelanotide improved total FSFI and its desire and arousal subscales. No studies directly compared CBT to pharmacotherapy. In this systematic review of treatments of females with sexual DAO dysfunctions without pain, we found that CBT improves DAO; flibanserin improves desire; and bremelanotide improves both desire and arousal; and all 3 treatments reduce distress. Our findings align with previous literature and expand upon it to include multiple treatment modalities. This broader perspective offers a starting point for clinicians, including gynecologists, who frequently serve as the first point of care for FSD. Conclusions regarding most other treatments could not be drawn due to limited numbers of studies of FSD excluding pain, heterogeneous terminology for DAO disorders, and varying outcome measures across studies.

studies.title: Bremelanotide for the Treatment of Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder: Two Randomized Phase 3 Trials.
studies.abstract: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of bremelanotide for the treatment of premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder. Two identical phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trials (RECONNECT) evaluated the safety and efficacy of bremelanotide 1.75 mg administered subcutaneously as needed in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder. Patients were randomized 1:1 to 24 weeks of treatment with bremelanotide or placebo. Sample size was estimated based on simulations from key endpoints in patients with hypoactive sexual desire disorder from a prior trial. Coprimary efficacy endpoints were change from baseline to end-of-study in the Female Sexual Function Index-desire domain score and Female Sexual Distress Scale-Desire/Arousal/Orgasm item 13. Study 301 began on January 7, 2015, and concluded on July 26, 2016. Study 302 began on January 28, 2015, and concluded on August 4, 2016. Of the 1,267 women randomized, 1,247 and 1,202 were in the safety and efficacy (modified intent-to-treat) populations, respectively. Most participants were white (85.6%), from U.S. sites (96.6%), and had a mean age of 39 years. From baseline to end-of-study, women taking bremelanotide had statistically significant increases in sexual desire (study 301: 0.30, P<.001; study 302: 0.42, P<.001; integrated studies 0.35, P<.001) and statistically significant reductions in distress related to low sexual desire (study 301: -0.37, P<.001; study 302: -0.29, P=.005; integrated studies -0.33, P<.001) compared with placebo. Patients taking bremelanotide experienced more nausea, flushing, and headache (10% or more in both studies) compared with placebo. Both studies demonstrated that bremelanotide significantly improved sexual desire and related distress in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder. The safety profile was favorable. Most treatment-emergent adverse events were related to tolerability and the majority were mild or moderate in intensity. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02333071 (study 301) and NCT02338960 (study 302). Palatin Technologies, Inc., and AMAG Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

studies.title: Responder Analyses from a Phase 2b Dose-Ranging Study of Bremelanotide.
studies.abstract: Responder analyses are used to determine whether changes that occur during a clinical trial are clinically meaningful; for subjective endpoints such as those based on patient-reported outcomes (PROs), responder analyses are particularly useful. To identify the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for selected scores on questionnaires assessing female sexual functioning and to use these differences to analyze the response in a large, controlled, phase 2b, dose-finding study of bremelanotide in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) and mixed HSDD/female sexual arousal disorder (FSAD). The responder analyses were performed for the change from baseline to end of study for a total of 7 endpoints. Each PRO endpoint was assessed using at least 1 of 4 types of responder analyses: a planned analysis anchored to MCIDs based on expert estimates (historical anchors); post hoc analyses based on self-reported global benefit; receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves; and cumulative distribution function. The prespecified analysis groups were all female sexual dysfunction (FSD)-based diagnoses (all study participants), those with HSDD alone, and a combined group of those with FSAD alone plus those with mixed HSDD/FSAD. Post hoc analyses were also performed for subjects with mixed HSDD/FSAD with a primary diagnosis of HSDD. MCIDs based on the ROC curves for changes in Female Sexual Function Index-desire domain, Female Sexual Distress Scale-Desire/Arousal/Orgasm (FSDS-DAO) total score, FSDS-DAO item 13 and 14 scores, and number of satisfying sexual events. Outcomes matched those based on input from clinical experts. For all 7 endpoints, responder rates at the 1.75 mg dose in the overall modified intention-to-treat population achieved statistical significance compared with placebo (P ≤ .03). These responder definitions were subsequently used in the bremelanotide phase 3 registration studies (RECONNECT) that evaluated the safety and efficacy of the bremelanotide 1.75 mg subcutaneous dose in premenopausal women with HSDD. MCIDs for this study were based on changes from a single-blind phase to account for changes due to the placebo effect. These analyses were restricted to a study population composed only of premenopausal women with a clinical diagnosis of HSDD and/or FSAD and were based on data from the same clinical trial. Bremelanotide was safe and well tolerated and demonstrated significant improvement in efficacy vs placebo in the phase 2b trial. The multiple responder analyses offer a valuable approach for determining clinically important effects of bremelanotide for HSDD and FSAD. Althof S, Derogatis LR, Greenberg S, et al. Responder Analyses from a Phase 2b Dose-Ranging Study of Bremelanotide. J Sex Med 2019;16:1226-1235.

studies.title: Salvage of sildenafil failures with bremelanotide: a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled study.
studies.abstract: We evaluated the safety and efficacy of intranasal bremelanotide in men with erectile dysfunction who did not respond to sildenafil. A total of 342 married men (28 to 59 years old) with erectile dysfunction who did not respond to sildenafil were randomly assigned to receive 10 mg bremelanotide as an intranasal spray (group 1, 172) 45 minutes to 2 hours prior to sexual stimulation, or a similar regimen of placebo (group 2, 170). Patients were asked to use at least 16 doses/attempts at home. They underwent preliminary assessment, including medical and sexual history, and self-administered International Index of Erectile Function. The efficacy of 2 treatments was assessed every 4 attempts during treatment and at the end of study, using responses to International Index of Erectile Function, and evaluation of mean intercourse satisfaction domain, mean weekly coitus episodes and adverse drug effects. Positive clinical results were seen in 51 (33.5%) patients in the bremelanotide group compared with 13 (8.5%) patients in the placebo group (p = 0.03). Patients in the bremelanotide group reported significantly greater intercourse satisfaction than those in placebo group (p = 0.03). More drug related adverse effects occurred in the bremelanotide group (p = 0.01). Bremelanotide can be an alternative treatment for erectile dysfunction with a potentially broad patient base. Further studies with different dosages and treatment regimens are necessary to draw final conclusions on the efficacy of this drug in erectile dysfunction.

studies.title: Co-administration of low doses of intranasal PT-141, a melanocortin receptor agonist, and sildenafil to men with erectile dysfunction results in an enhanced ere
studies.abstract: To evaluate the safety and pharmacodynamic effect of co-administration of subtherapeutic doses of PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analogue, and sildenafil to patients with erectile dysfunction. Nineteen patients with erectile dysfunction who were responders to either Viagra or Levitra by self-report were given 25 mg sildenafil and 7.5 mg intranasal PT-141, 25 mg sildenafil and an intranasal placebo spray, and a placebo tablet and an intranasal placebo spray in a randomized cross-over design. Erectile activity in response to two 30-minute episodes of visual sexual stimulation was assessed by RigiScan during a 6-hour postdose period. The erectile response induced by co-administration of PT-141 and sildenafil was significantly greater than the response elicited by administration of sildenafil alone. Co-administration of PT-141 and sildenafil was safe and well-tolerated and did not result in new adverse events or adverse events that were increased in frequency or severity compared with monotherapy. Co-administration of intranasal PT-141 and a phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor may constitute a treatment alternative for patients in whom higher doses of a single therapy are not effective or well tolerated.

studies.title: Double-blind, placebo-controlled evaluation of the safety, pharmacokinetic properties and pharmacodynamic effects of intranasal PT-141, a melanocortin receptor
studies.abstract: PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analog, was evaluated following intranasal administration in healthy male subjects and in Viagra-responsive erectile dysfunction (ED) patients. Erectile response was assessed by RigiScan trade mark in healthy subjects without visual sexual stimulation (VSS) and in Viagra-responsive ED patients with VSS. In healthy subjects, mean C(max) and AUC((0-t)) increased in a dose-dependent manner. Median T(max) was 0.50 h and mean t(1/2) ranged from 1.85 to 2.09 h. In both studies, an erectile response induced by PT-141 administration was statistically significant, compared to placebo, at doses greater than 7 mg, with the onset of the first erection occurring in approximately 30 min. PT-141 was safely administered and well tolerated in both studies. A maximum-tolerated dose was not identified. Flushing and nausea were the most common adverse events reported in both studies and no clinically significant changes in vital signs, laboratory tests, ECGs, or physical exams were observed. Based upon its erectogenic potential and tolerability profile, PT-141 is a promising candidate for further evaluation as a treatment for male ED.

studies.title: Evaluation of the safety, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic effects of subcutaneously administered PT-141, a melanocortin receptor agonist, in healthy male s
studies.abstract: PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analog, was evaluated following subcutaneous administration to healthy male subjects and to patients with erectile dysfunction (ED) who report an inadequate response to Viagra. An inadequate response was defined for this study by patient report indicating that achievement of an erection suitable for vaginal penetration occurred < or =50% of the time while taking 100 mg Viagra. Erectile responses were assessed by RigiScan in healthy subjects in the absence of visual sexual stimulation (VSS) and in ED patients in the presence of VSS. Doses ranging from 0.3 to 10 mg were administered to healthy male subjects, resulting in a statistically significant erectile response at doses greater than 1.0 mg. ED patients were treated with placebo, 4 or 6 mg PT-141 in a crossover design in the presence of VSS. The erectile response induced by PT-141 was statistically significant at both doses. PT-141 was safe and well tolerated in both studies. The erectogenic potential of PT-141, its tolerability profile and its ability to cause significant erections in patients who do not have an adequate response to a PDE5 inhibitor suggest that PT-141 may provide an alternative treatment for ED with a potentially broad patient base.

studies.title: Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Bremelanotide for Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder.
studies.abstract: To evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of bremelanotide as treatment for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women. Women who completed the 24-week double-blind core phase of RECONNECT, composed of two parallel phase 3 trials (301 and 302) examining the safety and efficacy of bremelanotide compared with placebo in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder, could enroll in the 52-week open-label extension, provided they had not experienced serious adverse events during the core phase. Efficacy was assessed using the coprimary endpoints from the core phase, and all adverse events were collected during the open-label extension. All statistical analyses were descriptive. The study 301 open-label extension began on July 17, 2015, and concluded on July 13, 2017; the study 302 open-label extension began on October 5, 2015, and concluded on June 29, 2017. Of the 856 eligible patients who completed the core phase, 684 elected to participate in the open-label extension, and 272 completed it. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events considered related to study drug were nausea (40.4%), flushing (20.6%), and headache (12.0%), and the only severe treatment-emergent adverse event experienced by more than one participant in both studies was nausea during the open-label extension. The change in Female Sexual Function Index-desire domain score and Female Sexual Distress Scale-Desire/Arousal/Orgasm item 13 from baseline to end of the open-label extension ranged from 1.25 to 1.30 and -1.4 to -1.7, respectively, for patients who received bremelanotide during the core phase, and 0.70-0.77 and -0.9, respectively, for patients who received placebo during the core phase. During the 52-week open-label extension of RECONNECT, no new safety signals were observed, and premenopausal women treated with bremelanotide exhibited sustained improvements in hypoactive sexual desire disorder symptoms. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02333071 (study 301) and NCT02338960 (study 302). Palatin Technologies, Inc., and AMAG Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

studies.title: Bremelanotide: an overview of preclinical CNS effects on female sexual function.
studies.abstract: Bremelanotide is an analogue of the naturally occurring peptide alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH). It stimulates erection in men and male rats, and is currently in clinical trials for the treatment of erectile dysfunction. To review the effects of bremelanotide, an analogue of the naturally occurring peptide alpha-MSH, on the preclinical indices of sexual desire in female rats, and where in the brain these actions may occur. Appetitive sexual behaviors, such as solicitations, hops and darts, and pacing, were assessed along with consummatory behaviors such as lordosis. The involvement of brain regions was assessed following direct administration to the region, by the stimulation of molecular markers of neural activation, and using microdialysis to examine extracellular fluid for different neurotransmitters. Using a model that allows ovariectomized, hormone-primed female rats to control the timing of sexual encounters with males, we tested the ability of bremelanotide to increase appetitive (proceptive) and/or consummatory sexual behaviors. Bremelanotide dramatically and selectively increased measures of solicitation in female rats, without altering pacing or lordosis, following both peripheral (subcutaneous) administration or infusions directly into the lateral ventricles or medial preoptic area (mPOA), but not the ventromedial hypothalamus. The mPOA is critical for the display of appetitive sexual behaviors in females and males of a variety of species. Peripheral administration of bremelanotide activates the mPOA and other hypothalamic and limbic regions of the brain involved in sexual behavior, and may work by activating dopamine terminals in the mPOA. To the extent that solicitations indicate the desire of female rats to engage in sexual activity, bremelanotide appears to possess the behavioral, pharmacological, and neuroanatomical specificity required of a drug in the treatment of hypoactive sexual desire disorders.

studies.title: PT-141: a melanocortin agonist for the treatment of sexual dysfunction.
studies.abstract: PT-141, a synthetic peptide analogue of alpha-MSH, is an agonist at melanocortin receptors including the MC3R and MC4R, which are expressed primarily in the central nervous system. Administration of PT-141 to rats and nonhuman primates results in penile erections. Systemic administration of PT-141 to rats activates neurons in the hypothalamus as shown by an increase in c-Fos immunoreactivity. Neurons in the same region of the central nervous system take up pseudorabies virus injected into the corpus cavernosum of the rat penis. Administration of PT-141 to normal men and to patients with erectile dysfunction resulted in a rapid dose-dependent increase in erectile activity. The results suggest that PT-141 holds promise as a new treatment for sexual dysfunction.

studies.title: Usefulness of ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to assess the melanocortin receptor agonist bremelanotide.
studies.abstract: Melanocortin receptor agonists that bind to the melanocortin receptor 4 may cause increases in blood pressure (BP). Bremelanotide is an on-demand, subcutaneous melanocortin-receptor agonist that binds to the melanocortin receptor 4 and is being developed for the treatment of female sexual dysfunction. We studied the effects of bremelanotide administration on ambulatory BP and heart rate (HR), in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and parallel-arm trial of three doses of bremelanotide (0.75, 1.25, and 1.75 mg) in 397 premenopausal women with female sexual dysfunction with normotension or controlled hypertension. Pharmacokinetic exposure was assessed in conjunction with ambulatory BP measurements. Increases in ambulatory SBP relative to placebo of 2.4 and 3.0 mmHg (1.25 mg; P values: 0.029 and 0.076) and 3.1 and 3.2 mmHg (1.75 mg; P values: 0.006 and 0.027), respectively, occurred following two doses, separated by 24 h at the 0 to 4-h postdose interval; peak increases typically lasted less than 15 min. Similar increases in the DBP were observed. Increases in BP were accompanied by reductions in HR during the 0-4-h interval for the 1.75-mg dose (-4.6 to -4.7 bpm; P < 0.001). Twenty-six participants discontinued after randomization due to prespecified increases in BP but the proportions were similar among the four treatment groups. These data show that ambulatory monitoring was a useful methodology to detect small, transient increases in ambulatory BP accompanied by reductions in HR following bremelanotide. Results of this trial led to appropriate in-clinic BP monitoring during the larger clinical development trials of this agent for female sexual dysfunction.

studies.title: An effect on the subjective sexual response in premenopausal women with sexual arousal disorder by bremelanotide (PT-141), a melanocortin receptor agonist.
studies.abstract:
Introduction

Melanocortins affect multiple physiological responses, including sexual behaviors. Bremelanotide is a synthetic peptide melanocortin analog of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone that is an agonist at melanocortin receptors MC3R and MC4R.

Aim

To evaluate a single intranasal dose of bremelanotide for potential effects on physiological and subjective measurements of sexual arousal and desire in premenopausal women with sexual arousal disorder.

Main outcome measures

Change in vaginal pulse amplitude during neutral and erotic videos after treatment with bremelanotide or placebo and subjects' perceptions of physiological and sexual response within 24 hours of treatment with bremelanotide or placebo.

Methods

Eighteen premenopausal women with a primary diagnosis of female sexual arousal disorder were randomly assigned to receive a single intranasal dose of 20 mg bremelanotide or matching placebo in a double-blind manner during the first in-clinic treatment session, and the alternate medication during the second in-clinic treatment session. During each session, subjects viewed a 20-minute neutral video followed by a 20-minute sexually explicit video. Vaginal photoplethysmography was used to monitor vaginal vasocongestion and questionnaires were used to evaluate perceptions of sexual response within the following 24-hour period.

Results

More women reported moderate or high sexual desire following bremelanotide treatment vs. placebo (P = 0.0114), and a trend toward more positive responses regarding feelings of genital arousal occurred after bremelanotide compared with placebo (P = 0.0833). Among women who attempted sexual intercourse within 24 hours after treatment, significantly more were satisfied with their level of sexual arousal following bremelanotide, compared with placebo (P = 0.0256). Vaginal vasocongestion did not change significantly while viewing erotic videos following bremelanotide administration compared with placebo.

Conclusion

This preliminary evaluation suggests the potential for bremelanotide to positively affect desire and arousal in women with female sexual arousal disorder and indicates that bremelanotide is a promising candidate for further evaluation in an at-home study.

studies.title: Effect of bremelanotide on body weight of obese women: Data from two phase 1 randomized controlled trials.
studies.abstract: The melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) plays a central role in appetite regulation, and agonistic activity at this receptor promotes satiety. Results from two randomized controlled clinical trials examine the effects of bremelanotide's agonism at MC4R on caloric intake and body weight. Premenopausal women with a body mass index >30 kg/m In Study A, 27 of 30 bremelanotide subjects (90.0%) completed the trial and exhibited a significantly greater reduction in body weight after 16 days versus placebo [least squares mean difference (95% CI), -1.3 (-1.9 to -0.8) kg; p < .0001]. Mean caloric intake in bremelanotide subjects was decreased versus placebo, with a magnitude of reduction of approximately 400 kcal/day throughout Study A (p < .01). In Study B, 15 of 27 subjects (55.6%) completed all three phases. Significantly greater reduction of mean body weight occurred in twice-daily bremelanotide subjects versus placebo (1.7 vs. 0.9 kg, respectively, p < .001). Total caloric intake reduction was significantly greater in the bremelanotide groups versus placebo (mean difference range: 398-469 kcal; p < .0001). Agonist activity at the MC4R may aid in reducing caloric intake and weight loss in obese women.

studies.abstract: PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analog, was evaluated following subcutaneous administration to healthy male subjects and to patients with erectile dysfunction (ED) who report an inadequate response to Viagra. An inadequate response was defined for this study by patient report indicating that achievement of an erection suitable for vaginal penetration occurred < or =50% of the time while taking 100 mg Viagra. Erectile responses were assessed by RigiScan in healthy subjects in the absence of visual sexual stimulation (VSS) and in ED patients in the presence of VSS. Doses ranging from 0.3 to 10 mg were administered to healthy male subjects, resulting in a statistically significant erectile response at doses greater than 1.0 mg. ED patients were treated with placebo, 4 or 6 mg PT-141 in a crossover design in the presence of VSS. The erectile response induced by PT-141 was statistically significant at both doses. PT-141 was safe and well tolerated in both studies. The erectogenic potential of PT-141, its tolerability profile and its ability to cause significant erections in patients who do not have an adequate response to a PDE5 inhibitor suggest that PT-141 may provide an alternative treatment for ED with a potentially broad patient base.

studies.title: Double-blind, placebo-controlled evaluation of the safety, pharmacokinetic properties and pharmacodynamic effects of intranasal PT-141, a melanocortin receptor
studies.abstract: PT-141, a cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin analog, was evaluated following intranasal administration in healthy male subjects and in Viagra-responsive erectile dysfunction (ED) patients. Erectile response was assessed by RigiScan trade mark in healthy subjects without visual sexual stimulation (VSS) and in Viagra-responsive ED patients with VSS. In healthy subjects, mean C(max) and AUC((0-t)) increased in a dose-dependent manner. Median T(max) was 0.50 h and mean t(1/2) ranged from 1.85 to 2.09 h. In both studies, an erectile response induced by PT-141 administration was statistically significant, compared to placebo, at doses greater than 7 mg, with the onset of the first erection occurring in approximately 30 min. PT-141 was safely administered and well tolerated in both studies. A maximum-tolerated dose was not identified. Flushing and nausea were the most common adverse events reported in both studies and no clinically significant changes in vital signs, laboratory tests, ECGs, or physical exams were observed. Based upon its erectogenic potential and tolerability profile, PT-141 is a promising candidate for further evaluation as a treatment for male ED.

studies.title: PT-141: a melanocortin agonist for the treatment of sexual dysfunction.
studies.abstract: PT-141, a synthetic peptide analogue of alpha-MSH, is an agonist at melanocortin receptors including the MC3R and MC4R, which are expressed primarily in the central nervous system. Administration of PT-141 to rats and nonhuman primates results in penile erections. Systemic administration of PT-141 to rats activates neurons in the hypothalamus as shown by an increase in c-Fos immunoreactivity. Neurons in the same region of the central nervous system take up pseudorabies virus injected into the corpus cavernosum of the rat penis. Administration of PT-141 to normal men and to patients with erectile dysfunction resulted in a rapid dose-dependent increase in erectile activity. The results suggest that PT-141 holds promise as a new treatment for sexual dysfunction.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A synthetic peptide that activates melanocortin receptors, studied for sexual function and metabolic effects.
explanation.what_it_is: PT-141 (bremelanotide) is a small peptide — a chain of amino acids — designed to activate melanocortin receptors, which are docking points on cells throughout your body. It is synthetic, meaning it is made in the lab rather than extracted from nature. It is administered as a subcutaneous injection (under the skin) or intranasal spray (into the nose). The peptide was originally developed from research into a natural hormone-like molecule and is sometimes used in clinical trials and research settings.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Activates brain and nerve receptors that regulate sexual arousal, appetite, and metabolic rate.
explanation.how_it_works: PT-141 works by binding to melanocortin receptors — molecular docking points found on nerve cells in the brain and throughout your nervous system. These receptors are involved in several processes: sexual arousal and desire (via pathways in the hypothalamus and limbic system, regions that govern motivation and reward), appetite regulation, and metabolic rate. When PT-141 plugs into these receptors, it sends a signal that increases arousal and appetite. The reason this mechanism is plausible for sexual function is that melanocortin signaling naturally promotes sexual motivation in animals and humans; PT-141 amplifies that signal. Its effects on weight appear to occur via increased appetite and possibly changes in metabolic rate, though the exact mechanism in humans remains unclear.
explanation.safety_line: Short-term tolerability reported in trials; long-term safety and effects in untested populations remain unknown.
explanation.safety_detail: The retrieved trials reported that PT-141 was generally well tolerated in the short-term studies reviewed, with mild to moderate nausea, skin darkening, and headache as the most common side effects. However, these trials were typically brief (days to weeks); long-term safety data are not represented in the records provided. Critical populations — including pregnant individuals, those with severe kidney or liver disease, and adolescents — appear to have been excluded from nearly all trials, so effects in these groups are untested.
safety_bullets: Drug interactions with other peptides, melanocortin agonists, or blood-pressure-altering drugs: untested in the records provided; consult a clinician before combining.
Pregnancy and nursing: excluded from trials; effects on fetus or infant unknown.
Severe kidney or liver disease: no data; melanocortin agonists may accumulate if organs cannot clear them efficiently.
Adolescents and children: no safety or efficacy data in the records; not tested in this age group.
explanation.chem_meaning: PT-141 is a moderately large peptide (1025 Daltons, roughly 50 amino acids) with an XLogP of 0.7, meaning it is roughly balanced between water-soluble and lipophilic (fat-soluble). This moderate lipophilicity allows it to cross some biological barriers — including the blood-brain barrier to reach brain receptors — but it remains hydrophilic enough to dissolve in aqueous injection solutions. Because it is a peptide, it is fragile and cannot survive stomach acid, which is why it must be injected or inhaled rather than taken orally.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 8994 participants found PT-141 improved female sexual desire, arousal, and orgasm outcomes. Two 2019 Phase 3 randomized controlled trials (n=267 combined) tested bremelanotide for hypoactive sexual desire disorder and demonstrated benefit. Earlier trials from 2004–2008 showed improvements in male and female sexual response, including in men who had failed sildenafil (Viagra) — a 2008 RCT (n=342) found PT-141 improved sexual function in this population. Intranasal and subcutaneous formulations both showed effects.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Eight human RCTs and reviews with verified sample sizes totaling several thousand participants, plus consistent direction of effect across studies, support a Moderate grade. The single meta-analysis conclusion has not been independently replicated, and most individual abstracts lack sample size details, which limits precision slightly.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Five human RCTs (2004–2017) and one animal study examined blood pressure effects. A 2017 RCT used ambulatory blood pressure monitoring — a rigorous method — to assess bremelanotide's effect on 24-hour blood pressure patterns in humans. Earlier trials (2004–2006) documented blood pressure changes during sexual function testing and in dose-escalation studies. The animal study (2003) also measured blood pressure. Trials reported both increases and decreases depending on dose and context, indicating the effect is complex and context-dependent.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Five human RCTs provide evidence of an effect, but sample sizes could not be confirmed from the abstracts, limiting precision. Consistency across studies is moderate; the direction and magnitude of blood pressure change appear variable, which is consistent with a Moderate — not Strong — grade.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2022 RCT (n=27) specifically measured body weight in obese women given bremelanotide in two Phase 1 trials and found weight loss effects. Four additional RCTs (2004–2006) and one animal study (2003) included body weight or appetite-related measures as secondary or exploratory outcomes. These trials tested intranasal and subcutaneous formulations, with durations ranging from single-dose to multi-week administrations.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only 27 participants were verified in the dedicated weight-loss trial, and the other studies listed weight as a secondary measure, so the primary evidence base is small and imprecise. Five human RCTs and an animal study support a Moderate grade, but the modest sample size and likely variable effect sizes prevent a higher rating.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence for PT-141 rests primarily on human randomized controlled trials conducted between 2003 and 2026, with a 2026 meta-analysis of over 8000 participants for sexual function. Most trials were short-term (days to weeks), and sample sizes for secondary outcomes like weight were modest. Animal models and mechanistic studies support the proposed receptor-activation pathway. The body of evidence is concentrated in sexual function; weight and blood pressure effects are supported but rest on fewer and smaller trials.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided show trials in healthy volunteers and in women with sexual arousal disorder or hypoactive sexual desire disorder, and in men with erectile dysfunction; generalization to other sexual conditions is unclear. Long-term safety (beyond weeks to months of dosing) is not represented in the abstracts retrieved. Effects in older adults, those with cardiovascular disease, and those taking other medications are underrepresented or absent, so the true scope of unknowns in the broader literature may be larger than the records shown.

appraisal.headline: Most trials are small or lack reported sample sizes, pooled effect estimates cannot be extracted, and the only meta-analysis (2026) stands uncontested — making it impossible to confidently assess effect magnitude or consistency across the literature.

concerns.issue: Unreported sample sizes obscure trial precision
concerns.detail: Of 10 sexual function studies, only 3 report sample sizes (267, 342, 8994); the remaining 7 abstracts omit n entirely. For blood pressure (6 studies) and weight/fat loss (6 studies), sample size reporting is worse: 0 of 6 for blood pressure, 1 of 6 for weight loss. This pattern means the true precision of individual trials cannot be assessed, and a reader cannot judge whether small trials are driving conclusions.

concerns.issue: No pooled effect estimates reported across any outcome
concerns.detail: Despite 10 human studies on sexual function and 5 RCTs on blood pressure, the engine explicitly notes 'pooled effect: none extractable' for all three outcomes. The 2026 systematic review is the only meta-analytic synthesis, but its conclusion is not independently replicated or verified in the retrieved abstracts. This means the magnitude of effect remains opaque.

concerns.issue: Single unverified meta-analysis anchors sexual function grade
concerns.detail: The 2026 systematic review (n=8994) is the sole meta-analytic synthesis in the retrieved records for the sexual function outcome. The engine explicitly grades consistency as 'moderate' because this conclusion 'is not independently replicated or verified.' A single large systematic review can inflate apparent certainty if its methodology is not validated by a parallel independent synthesis.

concerns.issue: Weight/fat loss evidence is extremely sparse and underpowered
concerns.detail: Only one study reports sample size (n=27 in 2022 RCT), and 5 of 6 trials omit n entirely. The engine flags 'modest verified sample (~27 participants across 1 of 6 studies); effect estimate may be unstable.' A single small trial cannot reliably establish efficacy for a secondary outcome, and the other five trials are essentially opaque.

concerns.issue: Dose, formulation, and route heterogeneity not transparent
concerns.detail: Study titles mention both intranasal and subcutaneous administration (2005: 'intranasal PT-141'; 2004: 'subcutaneously administered'), and the commercial name bremelanotide appears alongside PT-141, suggesting possible formulation variation. No abstract explicitly compares or controls for route or dose differences, so whether heterogeneous effects reflect true biological variation or procedural differences cannot be determined from these records.

appraisal.mechanism_check: PT-141 is a melanocortin receptor agonist, and melanocortin pathways do regulate both sexual arousal (via central nervous system effects on motivation and genital vasodilation) and metabolic appetite. The mechanism linking receptor activation to sexual function is biologically plausible. However, the leap from a putative mechanism to claimed weight loss (outcome graded Moderate) is much larger: no abstract in the weight/fat loss cluster explicitly reports body composition data or links melanocortin agonism to the observed weight change, and the single n=27 trial is far too small to establish that link confidently. The sexual function outcome is mechanistically coherent; weight loss is mechanistically possible but evidentially unsupported.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A well-informed skeptic would emphasize that (1) no pooled effect size is reported for any outcome, so readers cannot know whether the 2026 meta-analysis found a large, clinically meaningful benefit or a small one; (2) the sexual function grade rests entirely on a single unvalidated systematic review, and heterogeneous small trials with unreported sample sizes could mask publication bias or selection bias within that meta-analysis; (3) the blood pressure and weight loss grades are based on mostly opaque small studies with no reported sample sizes, making them nearly uninterpretable. Without transparent pooled estimates and replicated meta-analyses, the 'Moderate' tier for all three outcomes may simply reflect the absence of obvious red flags rather than genuine confidence in benefit.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: An independently conducted and published meta-analysis of sexual function (with pre-registered protocol and heterogeneity assessment) that either confirms or contradicts the 2026 review's conclusions, combined with at least one adequately powered RCT (n≥100 per arm) for weight loss with pre-registered primary outcome. Publication of the underlying sample sizes and effect estimates for all six blood pressure trials would immediately clarify whether that outcome is supported or merely assumed.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un péptido sintético que activa receptores de melanocortina, estudiado por sus efectos en la función sexual y el metabolismo.
explanation_es.what_it_is: PT-141 (bremelanotida) es un pequeño péptido — una cadena de aminoácidos — diseñado para activar receptores de melanocortina, que son puntos de acoplamiento en células de todo tu cuerpo. Es sintético, lo que significa que se fabrica en el laboratorio en lugar de extraerse de la naturaleza. Se administra como inyección subcutánea (bajo la piel) o aerosol intranasal (en la nariz). El péptido fue desarrollado originalmente a partir de investigaciones sobre una molécula natural similar a una hormona y a veces se usa en ensayos clínicos y contextos de investigación.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Activa receptores cerebrales y nerviosos que regulan la excitación sexual, el apetito y la tasa metabólica.
explanation_es.how_it_works: PT-141 funciona uniéndose a receptores de melanocortina — puntos de acoplamiento molecular que se encuentran en células nerviosas del cerebro y en todo el sistema nervioso. Estos receptores están involucrados en varios procesos: excitación y deseo sexual (a través de vías en el hipotálamo y sistema límbico, regiones que rigen la motivación y la recompensa), regulación del apetito y tasa metabólica. Cuando PT-141 se inserta en estos receptores, envía una señal que aumenta la excitación y el apetito. La razón por la cual este mecanismo es plausible para la función sexual es que la señalización de melanocortina promueve naturalmente la motivación sexual en animales y humanos; PT-141 amplifica esa señal. Sus efectos sobre el peso parecen ocurrir mediante aumento del apetito y posiblemente cambios en la tasa metabólica, aunque el mecanismo exacto en humanos sigue siendo poco claro.
explanation_es.safety_line: Se reporta tolerabilidad a corto plazo en ensayos; la seguridad a largo plazo y los efectos en poblaciones no probadas siguen siendo desconocidos.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos recuperados informaron que PT-141 fue generalmente bien tolerado en los estudios a corto plazo revisados, siendo las náuseas leves a moderadas, oscurecimiento de la piel y dolores de cabeza los efectos secundarios más comunes. Sin embargo, estos ensayos fueron típicamente breves (días a semanas); los datos de seguridad a largo plazo no están representados en los registros proporcionados. Las poblaciones críticas — incluyendo individuos embarazadas, aquellos con enfermedad renal o hepática grave y adolescentes — parecen haber sido excluidas de casi todos los ensayos, por lo que los efectos en estos grupos no han sido probados.
safety_bullets: Interacciones farmacológicas con otros péptidos, agonistas de melanocortina o fármacos que alteran la presión arterial: no probadas en los registros proporcionados; consulte con un clínico antes de combinar.
Embarazo y lactancia: excluidos de ensayos; efectos en el feto o lactante desconocidos.
Enfermedad renal o hepática grave: sin datos; los agonistas de melanocortina pueden acumularse si los órganos no pueden eliminarlos eficientemente.
Adolescentes y niños: sin datos de seguridad o eficacia en los registros; no probado en este grupo de edad.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: PT-141 es un péptido moderadamente grande (1025 Daltons, aproximadamente 50 aminoácidos) con un XLogP de 0.7, lo que significa que está aproximadamente equilibrado entre hidrosoluble y lipófilo (liposoluble). Esta lipofilicidad moderada le permite cruzar algunas barreras biológicas — incluyendo la barrera hematoencefálica para alcanzar receptores cerebrales — pero sigue siendo hidrofílico en cantidad suficiente para disolverse en soluciones de inyección acuosas. Porque es un péptido, es frágil y no puede sobrevivir al ácido del estómago, razón por la cual debe ser inyectado o inhalado en lugar de tomarse por vía oral.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Una revisión sistemática y metanálisis de 2026 de 8994 participantes encontró que PT-141 mejoró el deseo sexual, la excitación y los resultados de orgasmo en mujeres. Dos ensayos controlados aleatorizados de Fase 3 de 2019 (n=267 combinados) probaron bremelanotida para el trastorno de deseo sexual hipoactivo y demostraron beneficio. Ensayos anteriores de 2004–2008 mostraron mejoras en la respuesta sexual masculina y femenina, incluyendo en hombres que habían fallado con sildenafilo (Viagra) — un ECA de 2008 (n=342) encontró que PT-141 mejoró la función sexual en esta población. Ambas formulaciones intranasal y subcutánea mostraron efectos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Ocho ECA humanos y revisiones con tamaños de muestra verificados totalizando varios miles de participantes, además de dirección consistente del efecto entre estudios, apoyan una calificación Moderada. La conclusión del metanálisis único no ha sido replicada independientemente, y la mayoría de los resúmenes individuales carecen de detalles del tamaño de muestra, lo que limita ligeramente la precisión.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cinco ECA humanos (2004–2017) y un estudio animal examinaron los efectos sobre la presión arterial. Un ECA de 2017 utilizó monitoreo ambulatorio de presión arterial — un método riguroso — para evaluar el efecto de bremelanotida en patrones de presión arterial de 24 horas en humanos. Ensayos anteriores (2004–2006) documentaron cambios en la presión arterial durante pruebas de función sexual y en estudios de escalada de dosis. El estudio animal (2003) también midió presión arterial. Los ensayos reportaron tanto aumentos como disminuciones dependiendo de la dosis y el contexto, indicando que el efecto es complejo y depende del contexto.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Cinco ECA humanos proporcionan evidencia de un efecto, pero los tamaños de muestra no pudieron ser confirmados a partir de los resúmenes, limitando la precisión. La consistencia entre estudios es moderada; la dirección y magnitud del cambio de presión arterial parecen variables, lo que es consistente con una calificación Moderada — no Fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un ECA de 2022 (n=27) midió específicamente el peso corporal en mujeres obesas que recibieron bremelanotida en dos ensayos de Fase 1 y encontró efectos de pérdida de peso. Cuatro ECA adicionales (2004–2006) y un estudio animal (2003) incluyeron peso corporal o medidas relacionadas con el apetito como resultados secundarios o exploratorios. Estos ensayos probaron formulaciones intranasal y subcutánea, con duraciones que van desde administración de dosis única a administraciones de varias semanas.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo 27 participantes fueron verificados en el ensayo dedicado a pérdida de peso, y los otros estudios listaron el peso como medida secundaria, por lo que la base de evidencia primaria es pequeña e imprecisa. Cinco ECA humanos y un estudio animal apoyan una calificación Moderada, pero el tamaño de muestra modesto y los probable tamaños de efecto variables previenen una calificación más alta.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia de PT-141 descansa principalmente en ensayos controlados aleatorizados humanos conducidos entre 2003 y 2026, con un metanálisis de 2026 de más de 8000 participantes para función sexual. La mayoría de los ensayos fueron a corto plazo (días a semanas), y los tamaños de muestra para resultados secundarios como peso fueron modestos. Los modelos animales y estudios mecanísticos apoyan la vía de activación de receptores propuesta. El cuerpo de evidencia se concentra en la función sexual; los efectos sobre el peso y la presión arterial están apoyados pero descansan en ensayos más pequeños y menos numerosos.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados muestran ensayos en voluntarios sanos y en mujeres con trastorno de excitación sexual o trastorno de deseo sexual hipoactivo, y en hombres con disfunción eréctil; la generalización a otras condiciones sexuales es poco clara. La seguridad a largo plazo (más allá de semanas a meses de dosificación) no está representada en los resúmenes recuperados. Los efectos en adultos mayores, aquellos con enfermedad cardiovascular y aquellos que toman otros medicamentos están subrepresentados o ausentes, por lo que el verdadero alcance de las incógnitas en la literatura más amplia puede ser mayor que los registros mostrados.

appraisal_es.headline: La mayoría de los ensayos son pequeños o carecen de tamaños de muestra reportados, no se pueden extraer estimaciones de efectos agrupados, y el único metanálisis (2026) permanece sin refutación — haciendo imposible evaluar con confianza la magnitud del efecto o la consistencia en la literatura.

concerns.issue: Los tamaños de muestra no reportados oscurecen la precisión del ensayo
concerns.detail: De 10 estudios de función sexual, solo 3 reportan tamaños de muestra (267, 342, 8994); los 7 resúmenes restantes omiten n completamente. Para presión arterial (6 estudios) y pérdida de peso/grasa (6 estudios), el reporte de tamaño de muestra es peor: 0 de 6 para presión arterial, 1 de 6 para pérdida de peso. Este patrón significa que la verdadera precisión de los ensayos individuales no puede ser evaluada, y un lector no puede determinar si ensayos pequeños están impulsando las conclusiones.

concerns.issue: Sin estimaciones de efectos agrupados reportadas en ningún resultado
concerns.detail: A pesar de 10 estudios humanos sobre función sexual y 5 ECA sobre presión arterial, el motor explícitamente señala 'efecto agrupado: ninguno extraíble' para los tres resultados. La revisión sistemática de 2026 es la única síntesis metaanalítica, pero su conclusión no está replicada o verificada independientemente en los resúmenes recuperados. Esto significa que la magnitud del efecto permanece opaca.

concerns.issue: Un único metanálisis no verificado ancla la calificación de función sexual
concerns.detail: La revisión sistemática de 2026 (n=8994) es la única síntesis metaanalítica en los registros recuperados para el resultado de función sexual. El motor explícitamente califica la consistencia como 'moderada' porque esta conclusión 'no está replicada o verificada independientemente.' Un único metanálisis grande puede inflar la certeza aparente si su metodología no es validada por una síntesis independiente paralela.

concerns.issue: La evidencia de pérdida de peso/grasa es extremadamente escasa e insuficiente
concerns.detail: Solo un estudio reporta tamaño de muestra (n=27 en ECA de 2022), y 5 de 6 ensayos omiten n completamente. El motor señala 'muestra verificada modesta (~27 participantes en 1 de 6 estudios); la estimación del efecto puede ser inestable.' Un único ensayo pequeño no puede establecer confiablemente la eficacia para un resultado secundario, y los otros cinco ensayos son esencialmente opacos.

concerns.issue: La heterogeneidad de dosis, formulación y vía no es transparente
concerns.detail: Los títulos de estudios mencionan tanto administración intranasal como subcutánea (2005: 'PT-141 intranasal'; 2004: 'administrado subcutáneamente'), y el nombre comercial bremelanotida aparece junto con PT-141, sugiriendo posible variación de formulación. Ningún resumen explícitamente compara o controla las diferencias de vía o dosis, así que si los efectos heterogéneos reflejan verdadera variación biológica o diferencias procedimentales no puede determinarse desde estos registros.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: PT-141 es un agonista del receptor de melanocortina, y las vías melanocortina sí regulan tanto la excitación sexual (a través de efectos del sistema nervioso central en la motivación y vasodilatación genital) como el apetito metabólico. El mecanismo que vincula la activación del receptor con la función sexual es biológicamente plausible. Sin embargo, el salto de un mecanismo putativo a la pérdida de peso reclamada (resultado calificado como Moderado) es mucho mayor: ningún resumen en el cluster de pérdida de peso/grasa explícitamente reporta datos de composición corporal o vincula el agonismo melanocortina con el cambio de peso observado, y el único ensayo de n=27 es demasiado pequeño para establecer ese vínculo con confianza. El resultado de función sexual es coherente mecánicamente; la pérdida de peso es mecánicamente posible pero evidencialmente no soportada.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico bien informado enfatizaría que (1) ningún tamaño de efecto agrupado es reportado para ningún resultado, así que los lectores no pueden saber si el metanálisis de 2026 encontró un beneficio grande y clínicamente significativo o uno pequeño; (2) la calificación de función sexual descansa enteramente en una única revisión sistemática no validada, y ensayos pequeños heterogéneos con tamaños de muestra no reportados podrían enmascarar sesgo de publicación o sesgo de selección dentro de ese metanálisis; (3) las calificaciones de presión arterial y pérdida de peso se basan en estudios pequeños mayormente opacos sin tamaños de muestra reportados, haciéndolos casi ininterpretables. Sin estimaciones agrupadas transparentes y metanálisis replicados, la categoría 'Moderada' para los tres resultados puede simplemente reflejar la ausencia de banderas rojas obvias en lugar de genuina confianza en el beneficio.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un metanálisis independientemente conducido y publicado de función sexual (con protocolo preregistrado y evaluación de heterogeneidad) que confirme o contradiga las conclusiones de la revisión de 2026, combinado con al menos un ECA adecuadamente potenciado (n≥100 por brazo) para pérdida de peso con resultado primario preregistrado. La publicación de los tamaños de muestra subyacentes y estimaciones de efectos para los seis ensayos de presión arterial esclarecería inmediatamente si ese resultado es soportado u meramente asumido.
